method: A US basis weight is the weight in pounds of a 500-sheet ream of a grade's standard base sheet, so the tool converts through grams per square metre as the common currency. The base sheets are bond, writing and ledger at 17 by 22 inches (374 square inches), text, book and offset at 25 by 38 inches (950), cover at 20 by 26 inches (520), index at 25.5 by 30.5 inches (777.75), bristol at 22.5 by 28.5 inches (641.25) and tag at 24 by 36 inches (864). One square inch is exactly 0.00064516 square metres and one pound is exactly 453.59237 grams, so a pound value becomes grams per square metre by multiplying by 453.59237 and dividing by 500 base sheets times the base area in square metres, and the reverse multiplies by that same product instead. Results are rounded half up to one decimal place; the addition of a billionth before rounding keeps a binary value that should land exactly on a half, such as 49.95, from rounding downwards. Weights are accepted from 1 to 2,000 g/m2, which covers tissue to heavy board, and a pound entry that would exceed that metric ceiling is rejected rather than silently clipped. Caliper, thickness and bulk are out of scope because they are not derivable from weight: two sheets of the same grammage can differ in thickness as bulk varies. Everything runs in the browser, so nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere.

sources.title: US paper industry basis-weight convention: a 500-sheet ream of each grade's standard base sheet, with the bond, text, cover, index, bristol and tag sheet sizes used here.
ISO 536, Paper and board: determination of grammage, the g/m2 definition used for the metric side.
International yard and pound agreement (1959): one pound is exactly 453.59237 grams.
NIST Special Publication 811, Guide for the Use of the International System of Units: one inch is exactly 25.4 millimetres, so one square inch is 0.00064516 square metres.
Paper merchant weight charts used as an independent cross-check of the published examples, for example 80 lb text at about 118 g/m2 and 20 lb bond at about 75 g/m2.
